expectedTruths: Population (standardised, common-factor latent variables) effects on NB — SYSQ: direct 0.000000, indirect 0.245000, total 0.245000; INFQ: direct 0.000000, indirect 0.245500, total 0.245500; SERVQ: direct 0.000000, indirect 0.111500, total 0.111500; USE: direct 0.350000, indirect 0.090000, total 0.440000; SAT: direct 0.450000, indirect 0.000000, total 0.450000.

Population specific indirect effects on NB (product of path coefficients; they sum to each predecessor's indirect effect) — SYSQ -> USE -> SAT -> NB = 0.022500; SYSQ -> USE -> NB = 0.087500; SYSQ -> SAT -> NB = 0.135000; INFQ -> USE -> SAT -> NB = 0.018000; INFQ -> USE -> NB = 0.070000; INFQ -> SAT -> NB = 0.157500; SERVQ -> USE -> SAT -> NB = 0.009000; SERVQ -> USE -> NB = 0.035000; SERVQ -> SAT -> NB = 0.067500; USE -> SAT -> NB = 0.090000.

These population values are standardised effects among the latent variables. IPMA importance is the UNSTANDARDISED total effect on 0-100 rescaled construct scores estimated from the Likert sample, so it is compared engine-to-engine, not to these numbers; the ordering and signs (all positive) are expected to agree.
For every estimate and bootstrap draw: total effect = direct + sum of specific indirect effects (algebraic identity of recursive linear models).
Agreement profiles differ by construct (INFQ high-agreement, SAT mild-agreement, SERVQ low-agreement, others symmetric), so INFQ items have the highest and SERVQ items the lowest performance.
